**Limitations of Rutherford's Model**

Rutherford is the first scientist to introduce the idea of a nucleus and orbits of an electron. Although his model is the first acceptable atomic model, it has some limitations. They are:

a. Rutherford's model did not give any idea about the size and shape of the orbits along which the electrons move.

b. Planets in the solar system are electrically neutral but electrons and nucleus are charged. A parallelism between some charge neutral elements and charged elements is not quite correct.

c. There is no satisfactory explanation regarding how the electron will move round the nucleus in the case of atoms having more than one electron.

d. According to Maxwell's electromagnetic theory of radiation, any charged particle moving in a circular path, always emits energy and its radius will gradually grow smaller. At a stage, it is supposed to fall into the nucleus. That will be the end of the atom or at least its stability will be in trouble. However, that doesn't happen in nature; in other words, according to Maxwell's theory, Rutherford's atomic model is not correct.

**3.6.2 Bohr's Atomic Model**

Scientist Neils Bohr gave some corrections to Rutherford's atomic model in 1913. This corrected model is called the Bohr's atomic model. The main postulates of this model are:

a. The electron moves around the nucleus in a circular motion, about an axis. This circular motion is called an energy level or orbit. They are also known as

**3.6.2.1 সৃজনশীল প্রশ্ন / CQ**

**উদ্দীপক / STIMULUS**: What is the main difference between Rutherford's atomic model and Bohr's atomic model?

(ক) Rutherford's model does not explain how the electron will move round the nucleus in the case of atoms having more than one electron.
(খ) Bohr's model explains how the electron will move round the nucleus in the case of atoms having more than one electron.
(গ) Rutherford's model does not give any idea about the size and shape of the orbits along which the electrons move.
(ঘ) Bohr's model gives an idea about the size and shape of the orbits along which the electrons move.

**উত্তর / ANSWER**: (ক) Rutherford's model does not explain how the electron will move round the nucleus in the case of atoms having more than one electron.
